subcommittees.name: Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation Subcommittee

dimensions.assessment: Affects vessel operators, owners of nationalized foreign properties, and individuals operating in targeted maritime trade routes.
Can block vessel entry and operations in U.S. ports until disputes are resolved or compensation is provided.
dimensions.evidence: authorizes the President to prohibit the entry of a vessel into the United States if the vessel has transited any U.S. port

dimensions.assessment: No specific federal spending or revenue amounts are stated in the source text.
Amends title 46 of the United States Code to add new presidential powers regarding vessel entry restrictions and exemptions.
dimensions.evidence: amend title 46, United States Code, with respect to the types of vessels that may enter or operate in navigable waters

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory change with effects lasting until presidential conditions or dispute resolutions are met.
dimensions.evidence: The prohibition ends when the President determines that... the applicable country has restored ownership

missing_information: Exact fiscal costs or revenue impacts
The number of vessels or U.S. entities directly impacted
importance_detail.rationale: The bill grants the President authority to prohibit entry of certain vessels tied to nationalized or expropriated property in Western Hemisphere free trade partner countries, affecting specific maritime transport and property owners.
